questions.q: Why does the `incident` table already have fields like `short_description`, `state`, and `assignment_group` before you add anything?
options: ServiceNow hard-codes those fields separately on every ITSM table
Those fields only exist because a System Administrator manually added them
Because `incident` extends `task`, which defines those fields once for incident, problem, change, and request item alike
Incident does not actually inherit any fields from another table
questions.explain: Table inheritance means incident, problem, change, and request item all extend the same `task` parent, so core fields are defined once.

questions.q: What are the six real out-of-box values on `incident.state`?
options: Open, Pending, Escalated, Fixed, Archived, Rejected
New, In Progress, On Hold, Resolved, Closed, Canceled
New, Assigned, Working, Done, Closed, Deleted
Draft, Submitted, Approved, Active, Complete, Closed
questions.explain: These six values are the real out-of-box incident state model.

questions.q: Why should a well-implemented instance require a real Hold Reason value whenever State is set to On Hold?
options: Hold Reason is only cosmetic and has no reporting value
ServiceNow requires Hold Reason on every state, not just On Hold
Hold Reason replaces the need for a State field entirely
Without it, nobody can later tell what a stuck incident is actually waiting on — Awaiting Caller, Awaiting Change, or Awaiting Vendor
questions.explain: On Hold without a reason makes it impossible to report on what's actually blocking resolution.

questions.q: A well-implemented instance uses a Data Policy to require which two fields before an incident can move to Resolved?
options: Assignment Group and Priority
Resolution Code and Close Notes
Caller and Category
Short Description and Urgency
questions.explain: A Data Policy conditioned on State = Resolved makes Resolution Code and Close Notes mandatory only at that point in the lifecycle.

questions.q: Why is it a problem for an instance to allow an incident to move directly from New to Closed?
options: It skips Resolved, the state where the resolution evidence is recorded, leaving a closed incident with no record of what fixed it
It is not actually a problem — Closed and Resolved mean the same thing
New incidents are not allowed to have a Priority value
Only Canceled incidents are permitted to skip states
questions.explain: Resolved is where resolution evidence (Resolution Code, Close Notes) is captured; skipping it loses that record.
